source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Login to WebUI and go to KVM page.
2. Open multiple KVM page.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
User can open the numbers of KVM which should match the design.
EX: spec show it can open three remote KVM, then you can open to three KVM but not four.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- not runnable by agent: the "KVM Multiple user" check requires several users opening BMC KVM sessions simultaneously and observing the allowed connection count; this needs multiple interactive GUI clients and is not scriptable.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: operator opens multiple KVM sessions to verify the concurrent-user limit and behavior; agent cannot drive multiple GUI KVM clients.

historical_reviews.deepseek: NO correctly identifies the multiple-interactive-client boundary, but it does not distinguish tabs from independent server-side KVM sessions, define distinct-account versus same-account coverage, specify the design maximum and limit-plus-one behavior, or protect against conflicting input and incomplete cleanup.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: MANUAL ONLY / IMPROVED correctly adds admitted/rejected/queued/read-only/takeover outcomes and input arbitration. V3.1 further requires unique client/session IDs, account/role and source-IP dimensions, video stream independence, privilege/audit behavior and proof that closing every session releases capacity.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 907/2291 retains manual status but gives no client/account/session matrix, target identity, exact over-limit response, arbitration, audit or cleanup evidence.
historical_reviews.related_source_cases: The preceding keyboard/mouse case tests single-session input fidelity and does not establish concurrent capacity. Generic WebUI login concurrency is not equivalent to KVM video-session admission.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No sequence-1069, Wistron-BMC-00198-V002 or 60fd0a0afaee7846 draft exists in the invalidated run.
historical_reviews.v3: No V3 overlay exists for this case.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves the design-limit example; ED-34 treats maximum, account/client matrix and policy as Project inputs; ED-35 prohibits unsafe competing input or destructive actions; ED-38 preserves audit evidence, disallows automatic retry and retains engineer verdict ownership.

original_test_intent: Manually verify the BMC remote-KVM server enforces its Project-approved concurrent-session capacity for the same target, admits sessions through the supported limit, applies the designed view/input ownership policy and handles limit-plus-one predictably without corrupting existing sessions.
original_method: Use independent authorized KVM clients with an approved account/role matrix to open distinct server-side sessions to the verified BMC/SUT, one at a time through the documented maximum, then attempt one additional session. Observe admission, video continuity, view/input arbitration, audit records and capacity release after orderly closure.
manual_activity: Multiple authorized operators or independently controlled GUI clients must establish real KVM sessions and visually confirm video and any permitted input behavior. The agent may coordinate the matrix and collect logs but cannot substitute one tab/process for independent users without proving server-side sessions. Engineering supplies the capacity/policy and owns the verdict.
required_inputs: BMC/SUT identity, BMC/KVM firmware, supported client/browser/plugin versions and network paths
Approved maximum simultaneous KVM sessions and whether the limit is global, per target, per account, per role or per source
Authorized distinct accounts/roles, client endpoints/source IPs and expected session IDs
Admission and over-limit policy: reject, queue, view-only, takeover, preempt or another defined response
Shared/exclusive input ownership, safe marker/actions, video continuity, latency and existing-session impact criteria
Idle/session timeout, logout/abnormal-close handling and time allowed for capacity release
Screenshot/recording, KVM session table, BMC audit and client console/network evidence plan
safety_requirements: Do not clear BMC audit, KVM session, browser or host logs; concurrent admission and cleanup must remain traceable.
Verify all clients point to the same approved BMC and SUT, but use distinct authenticated sessions; multiple tabs sharing one session token do not prove multiple-user capacity.
Do not share credentials when the policy requires unique accounts, bypass role restrictions, disable session security or expose console contents in evidence.
Prevent simultaneous uncontrolled input. Use a safe test surface, nominate an input owner and prohibit power/reset, BIOS/firmware, destructive shell and credential actions.
Do not repeatedly reconnect after an over-limit response; preserve the first rejection/queue/takeover behavior and impact on existing sessions.
Close every admitted/queued session and verify capacity, locks and audit state recover without rebooting BMC or DUT; stop on unintended preemption, lost console or wrong-target input.
agent_execution_scope: Prepare the approved capacity and client/account/role/source matrix, session labels, safe-input ownership, evidence timestamps and cleanup/stop conditions; do not impersonate unavailable independent GUI operators.
Collect BMC session/audit tables and per-client browser/network metadata while operators open sessions sequentially through the limit and one beyond it.
Correlate each unique session ID with admission state, video continuity, view/input policy, latency and effects on prior sessions; record exact over-limit behavior.
Verify orderly closure and capacity release, archive redacted evidence and perform no credential/policy/power change, log clear, automatic retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Provide the authoritative KVM concurrency maximum, scope and supported client/account/role matrix.
Approve admission, over-limit, arbitration, timeout and capacity-recovery acceptance plus safe concurrent-input controls.
Supervise the interactive clients, confirm each real session and issue the formal verdict for limit, limit-plus-one and cleanup behavior.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The manual conclusion fits the unavailable multi-GUI client path, but its note does not prove independent server-side sessions or define the maximum, user/account scope, input policy, over-limit result, existing-session impact and cleanup.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No single CLI command substitutes for this UI policy test. Establish labeled independent KVM clients and authenticated sessions sequentially to the approved maximum plus one while capturing server session/audit data and safe visual evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The multiple-KVM WebUI action, design-matched count Criteria, example limit of three/not four, no Script, DeepSeek NO and 1/0-minute estimates remain preserved; the example is not promoted to a universal maximum.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Execute a capacity matrix with unique clients/accounts/session IDs for 1..L and L+1, verifying admission, video and arbitration on every existing session, then close sessions in a defined order and prove capacity release.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected BMC remote-KVM implementation and Project-supported client/account/network combinations.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC/KVM firmware, browser/client/plugin, client OS/source network, identity provider/session policy and SUT display versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Project BMC/KVM capacity and security specification, vendor remote-console/session manual and RBAC/audit policy.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Turns vague multiple pages into distinct auditable server sessions with limit-plus-one and cleanup verification while preserving manual interaction.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: One account with many tabs may not test multiple users; capacity alone does not prove long-term stability, input fidelity, RBAC isolation or performance under unrelated WebUI load.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Authoritative limit/scope, client-account-role matrix, exact policy outcomes, safe input control and cleanup evidence.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Concurrent controllers can interfere with the SUT, expose console data or preempt sessions; cookies/session reuse can make apparent clients share one backend session.

project_override_considerations: An approved KVM automation harness may coordinate multiple real client processes only if unique server-side sessions, identities, visual streams, input policy and cleanup are proven and engineer-approved. It must retain human visual confirmation for arbitration or display anomalies. Multiple tabs or API session counts alone are partial evidence, not automatic equivalence.
expected_evidence: BMC/SUT/KVM/client version identities and authoritative capacity/scope plus account-role-source-client matrix
For sessions 1..L and L+1: unique client/session ID, account/role/source, timestamps, admission/rejection/queue/view-only/takeover state and redacted KVM screenshot
Existing-session video continuity, latency/disconnect and safe input ownership/arbitration evidence during each new admission and over-limit attempt
BMC KVM session table/audit logs plus client console/network evidence showing first over-limit behavior without retry
Ordered close/logout and capacity-release proof, no credential/policy/power/log mutation, explicit untested combinations and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title, Procedure and Criteria consistently target KVM concurrent-session capacity and give a coherent design-specific example. The exact limit and scope are Project readiness inputs rather than contradictory source semantics.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The multi-user KVM capacity purpose and manual operation are clear. Project capacity/policy data and authorized clients can make execution ready, so missing inputs do not make the review permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps the correct manual boundary and adds independent-session identity, capacity scope, over-limit behavior, arbitration and cleanup evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on MANUAL ONLY and strengthens session-token/account/source identity, existing-session impact and capacity-release verification.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces generic photos with a server-audited 1..L and L+1 matrix and safe input ownership.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Keeps single-session keyboard/mouse fidelity and long-duration stability outside this capacity verdict.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No invalid draft exists for this case.

review_improvement: Prevents multiple tabs sharing one cookie, an undocumented limit or a screenshot of only the newest client from being reported as multi-user KVM capacity, and ensures over-limit and cleanup do not silently disrupt existing sessions.
independent_technical_reasoning: Concurrent KVM capacity is enforced by server-side session policy, not the number of visible browser tabs. Authentication reuse, account scope and source limits can change the effective count. Valid evidence therefore needs distinct backend session IDs through L+1, continuous observation of earlier sessions, defined input ownership and verified resource release after closure.
